articles.headline: Eckes and McAnally-Hilgemann Winter Talks Continue as Offseason Opens
articles.dek: Conversations regarding Christian Eckes and his future with McAnally-Hilgemann Racing advance as the winter break begins.
articles.body:
The offseason is underway, and garage chatter immediately centers on driver and team alignments for the upcoming campaign. Christian Eckes finished the 2027 season fifth in the standings with 774 points and two victories, capping off his year with a third-place run at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Sources close to the organization indicate that discussions between Eckes and McAnally-Hilgemann Racing have progressed from initial whispers into active talks regarding the direction of the program for next year.

Eckes delivered a consistent year behind the wheel, maintaining a high level of performance that kept him in the championship conversation deep into the schedule. Team management and the driver are evaluating equipment updates and crew configurations to ensure stronger contention from the opening round next spring. Nothing is signed yet, but insiders suggest both sides are motivated to finalize an agreement before testing dates are announced.

Elsewhere in the garage, teams facing performance pressure are assessing potential adjustments to driver rosters and crew chief pairings. Several organizations that struggled with high numbers of DNFs during the 25-race schedule are expected to make structural changes. The winter window provides the primary opportunity to lock in new sponsorships and complete driver contracts before the next wave of competition begins.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

articles.headline: Riggs Claims the Title Through Consistency While Honeycutt Falls Short
articles.dek: A statistical review of how Layne Riggs locked down the championship against a persistent Kaden Honeycutt.
articles.body:
The 2027 sim racing season is officially in the books following the finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Looking back at the full body of work across 25 races, Layne Riggs secured the championship crown by accumulating 877 total points and pacing the field with 5 victories. His average performance and steady accumulation of stage and finish points kept him ahead of the chasing pack from the regular season through the final checkered flag.

Kaden Honeycutt pushed the champion all year long, finishing second in the final standings with 837 points and four wins to his credit. Gio Ruggiero rounded out the top three positions in the final table with 817 points and three triumphs. Meanwhile, Ben Rhodes added a final victory to his ledger at Homestead, driving the number 99 machine to a 94-lap performance from the front, bringing his season total to two wins and 783 points for fourth overall.

The cutoff battle for The Chase proved decisive back at race 18, where Kris Wright secured the tenth and final playoff spot with 681 points, edging out Tyler Ankrum who missed the cut by finishing eleventh with 658 points. Wright's two victories during the campaign proved vital in holding off drivers attempting to chase down that final transfer spot during the summer stretch.

At the back end of the top sixteen, drivers like Mini Tyrrell finished the year with 569 points after 25 rounds of hard competition. Teams now turn their attention away from the track and toward the winter months to prepare equipment for the next season.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Rhodes Dominates Homestead Finale to Win Craftsman 200
articles.dek: Ben Rhodes drove to a dominant victory in the season-ending race at Homestead-Miami Speedway, leading 94 laps on the intermediate oval.
articles.body:
Ben Rhodes secured his second win of the season by capturing the checkered flag at the Craftsman 200 at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Rhodes started from the eighth position and powered his way to the front, pacing the field for 94 of the 200 laps in a clean display of speed. The race featured eight caution periods, but Rhodes managed every restart cleanly to hold off Stewart Friesen at the finish line by 1.441 seconds.

Stewart Friesen mounted a charge from the 18th starting spot to finish second. Friesen led 22 laps and capitalized on late race strategy and tire management to secure the runner up position. Christian Eckes crossed the line third after leading 21 laps, capping off a strong run that saw him stay near the front for most of the afternoon. King Robinson finished fourth after starting on the front row and leading 20 laps, while Grant Enfinger rounded out the top five after advancing from his 17th place starting spot.

Further down the order, Layne Riggs wrapped up his championship season with a solid sixth place finish, cementing his spot at the top of the final standings with 877 points and five wins. Kaden Honeycutt finished eighth to secure second in the final points tally with 837 points, followed by Gio Ruggiero in third overall. At the back of the lead pack, attrition claimed a few trucks as Jake Garcia exited due to an accident, while Brenden Queen and Andrés Pérez de Lara both dropped out with overheating issues.

The season concludes with this 25th event, sending the teams into the offseason to prepare for the next campaign. The garage will now shift its focus toward team adjustments, driver evaluations, and winter shop work before the trucks return to the track.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Silly Season Shakes Up the FedEx Freight Truck Series Grid for 2027
articles.dek: The offseason shuffling is complete as new driver pairings and garage moves set the stage for the 2027 season opener.
articles.body:
The garage doors are up and the preseason is here. The FedEx Freight Truck Series silly season brought plenty of movement across the pit lane, reshaping the grid before a single lap has been turned for 2027.

Tricon Garage headline the changes by bolstering their lineup. James Baker steps up to the Craftsman Truck Series to pilot the #5 truck after previously racing with Joe Gibbs Racing. He is joined at Tricon by Nicholas Hoggeton, who moves up from Nitro Motorsports to take over the #1 entry. These additions give Tricon a fresh look as they chase speed right out of the box.

Front Row Motorsports also enters the new year with a revamped stable. King Robinson moves up to the Truck Series to drive the #38 machine following a stint with Nitro Motorsports. Meanwhile, Chandler Smith departs Front Row to climb the ladder, moving up to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series with Sam Hunt Racing in the #26.

Further down the pit lane, John Verstappen advances to the Craftsman Truck Series with Niece Motorsports, sliding into the #42 truck after parting ways with Shearer Speed Racing. Grant Enfinger is listed with Halmar Friesen Racing in the #62 entry following his departure from CR7 Motorsports.

These adjustments mean new crew pairings will face immediate pressure. With the season about to start, every team must find speed quickly to avoid falling behind in a deep and competitive field.
articles.author: Marcy Teague

chase.headline: Early Look at the Projected Grid
chase.summary: Looking back at the completed 25 races, the simulated baseline numbers point to Layne Riggs holding the top spot with 877 points and a 100 percent lock on the title. Kaden Honeycutt and Gio Ruggiero round out the top three projections, though the field ultimately chased Riggs all year.

notes.layne riggs: Riggs leads the projection with 877 points and secured the top spot in the simulated standings.
notes.kaden honeycutt: Honeycutt sits second in the projections with 837 points, anchoring the front tier.
notes.gio ruggiero: Ruggiero locked down third in the final projections with 817 points.

race.headline: Season Finale Recap
race.summary: The final rounds saw strong performances across the board, with drivers making big charges through the pack. Ben Rhodes controlled the finale from the front to take a clean victory.

notes.ben rhodes: Rhodes controlled the race from the front and secured a clean victory.
notes.stewart friesen: Friesen put together a hard charging drive from 18th to finish second.
notes.tyler ankrum: Ankrum charged from P19 to finish third after leading 40 laps.

season.headline: Looking Back at Twenty-Five Rounds
season.summary: When you look at how this twenty-five race schedule played out, consistency won the day. Riggs never relinquished his grip on the top spot while others battled for every remaining position.

notes.layne riggs: Riggs proved untouchable all season, taking the top projection with 877 points.
notes.kris wright: Wright showed speed by capturing a win at Black's Tire 200.
notes.ty majeski: Majeski finally broke through to end a 21-race winless drought.
